title: Inducing Branching Morphogenesis in Human Cholangiocyte and Cholangiocarcinoma Organoids
author: Ober, Roos, et al.
materials: Cultrex PathClear Reduced Growth Factor BME

Timing: 3–4 weeks
1.All commercially available components and (conditioned) media should be aliquoted and applied in the correct concentrations before (BR)ICO cultures are initiated, according to the manufacturer’s recommendations (see materials and equipment for details).2.Generate conditioned medium (CM) for organoid culture by culturing stably transfected L-Wnt-3a, 293T-HA-Rspo1-Fc and Noggin HEK293 cell lines, for the production of Wnt-3a, R-Spondin and Noggin.1,2,4,5a.Twice a week, split or harvest the attached monolayer of cells upon 90%–100% confluency when log phase growth expansion is observed, not exceeding >10% debris or detached cells.i.Harvest medium by transferring into a 50 mL Falcon tube.ii.Centrifuge the collected media at 453 g for 5 min at 4°C.iii.Filter the supernatant through a 0.22 μm filter to avoid transfer of cells and debris.iv.Aliquot in 35 mL and store at −20°C (R-Spondin, Noggin) or 4°C (Wnt-3a) until further use.Note: Pool multiple batches to minimize variation in efficiency levels per batch round.b.Validate the quality and concentration of the harvested condition medium by applying ELISA (R-Spondin, Noggin) and the FOP-TOP assay (Wnt-3a), according to published instructions.3,6c.Every 3 months, check the cell lines for mycoplasma infection or other contaminations.Note: Basic culture experience and skills are preferential in order to plan and organize the collection of CM. This is especially critical for the timing of the first batch collection.Note: After cell line thawing and culture initiation, it is strongly recommended to let the HEK293T cells recover for at least two passages before the first batch of CM is harvested. Especially Noggin HEK293 can present itself as a poorly adhesive line directly after thawing, make sure to handle the cells gently upon washing.Note: Do not use CM-producing cell lines from which the media is harvested for further culture or seeding of new CM-producing batch, since these cells have been exhausted. Maintain a back-bone of the CM-producing cell line in culture, that can be used for seeding a fresh CM-producing badge for media harvest.Note: All three CM-producing cell lines can be long-term cultured until at least passage 80. It is recommended to perform (STR) genotyping when cell line exceeds passage 50, to ensure a representative cell line.Note: R-Spondin and Noggin CM can be stored long-term for at least one year in aliquots of 35 mL at −20°C, while R-Spondin and Noggin maintaining stable activity, including endurance of multiple freeze-thaw cycles. Additionally, 35 mL aliquoted Wnt-3a only remains stable for 3 months at 4°C.Note: Apply the CM according to the appropriate concentrations as mentioned in the culture protocol. If any divergent concentrations are measured during validation experiments, the amount added to the media should be amended accordingly.3.Prepare the required organoid culture medium and filter through a 0.22 μm filter before use.
Note: Organoid culture media can be stored for 1 week at 4°C, after which fresh organoid culture medium should be prepared.
Note: All culture media added to the ICO, SEM, EM or BM, should be pre-warmed to 37°C before addition to the culture wells and BME domes. Upon cold media addition, the BME domes will disintegrate into a more liquid state while losing its ICO supportive matrix capabilities, and dispatches from the well bottom.

steps.title: Prepare stock solutions and reagents
steps.instruction: Aliquot all commercial components at the concentrations recommended by the manufacturers and prepare the 0.1 % BSA in D‑PBS stock solution.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 50 mg BSA in 50 mL sterile Dulbecco’s Phosphate‑Buffered Saline (D‑PBS), filter through a 0.22 µm filter and store at 4 °C for up to six months or at –20 °C for up to one year.
Label and store all other aliquoted reagents according to the amounts and concentrations listed in the Materials table.

steps.title: Generate conditioned medium (CM)
steps.instruction: Produce Wnt‑3a, R‑Spondin and Noggin conditioned media from the respective stably transfected HEK293 cell lines.

substeps.instruction: Maintain each producer cell line (L‑Wnt‑3a, 293T‑HA‑Rspo1‑Fc, 293T‑HA‑Noggin) in DMEM + 89 % (500 mL) FBS + 10 % (50 mL) Penicillin‑Streptomycin (10 000 U/mL) + 1 % (5 mL) UltraGlutamine, adding the appropriate selection antibiotic (G418 500 µg/mL for Noggin, Zeocin 300 µg/mL for R‑Spondin, Zeocin 125 µg/mL for Wnt‑3a).
Twice weekly, when cultures reach 90 %–100 % confluency with <10 % debris, split or harvest the monolayer.
Collect the medium into a 50 mL Falcon tube, centrifuge at 453 g for 5 min at 4 °C, and filter the supernatant through a 0.22 µm filter.
Aliquot filtered supernatant into 35 mL portions: store R‑Spondin and Noggin CM at –20 °C, store Wnt‑3a CM at 4 °C. Pool multiple batches to reduce batch‑to‑batch variation.
Validate each CM batch by ELISA for R‑Spondin and Noggin and by the FOP‑TOP assay for Wnt‑3a; adjust concentrations in downstream media if validation deviates from expected levels.
Every 3 months, test all producer cell lines for mycoplasma and other contaminations.
After thawing a new cell line, allow at least two passages before harvesting the first CM batch; avoid using the same cells for both CM harvest and subsequent seeding.
Maintain a backup culture of each producer line (up to passage 80); perform STR genotyping after passage 50.

steps.title: Validate CM quality and monitor contamination
steps.instruction: Confirm activity of each conditioned medium and keep the producer lines free of contamination.

substeps.instruction: Perform ELISA for R‑Spondin and Noggin on each batch; perform the FOP‑TOP assay for Wnt‑3a.
Record concentrations and, if necessary, adjust the volume added to downstream organoid media to achieve the target final concentrations.
Screen producer lines for mycoplasma every 3 months and discard any contaminated cultures.

steps.title: Prepare organoid culture media
steps.instruction: Make the four organoid media (SEM, EM, BM, FM) using the listed reagents, filter through a 0.22 µm filter, store as indicated, and pre‑warm to 37 °C before use.

substeps.instruction: Start‑Expansion Medium (SEM): combine 4.18 mL ADV+++ (41 %), 5 µL A83‑01 (5 µM), 10 µL B27 (2 %), 50 ng/mL EGF (10 µL of 100 µg/mL stock), 100 ng/mL FGF10 (10 µL of 100 µg/mL stock), 10 µM Forskolin (10 µL of 10 mM stock), 10 µM Gastrin I (10 µL of 10 µM stock), 0.1 % hES Cell Cloning and Recovery (10 µL of 1000×), 25 ng/mL HGF (10 µL of 50 µg/mL stock), 1 % N2 (10 µL of 50×), 1.25 mM N‑Acetyl‑L‑Cystein (20 µL of 500 mM stock), 10 nM Nicotinamide (10 µL of 1 M stock), 25 ng/mL Noggin CM (1 mL of 10 % stock), 1 mM R‑Spondin CM (1 mL of 10 % stock), 0.3 nM Wnt‑3a CM (3.33 mL of 10 % stock), 10 µM Y‑27632 (10 µL of 10 mM stock). Total volume 10 mL. Store at 4 °C for ≤1 week.

Expansion Medium (EM): combine 85 % ADV+++ (85 mL), 5 µM A83‑01 (5 µL), 2 % B27 (2 mL), 50 ng/mL EGF (100 µL of 100 µg/mL stock), 100 ng/mL FGF10 (100 µL of 100 µg/mL stock), 10 µM Forskolin (100 µL of 10 mM stock), 10 nM Gastrin I (100 µL of 10 µM stock), 25 ng/mL HGF (100 µL of 50 µg/mL stock), 1 % N2 (1 mL of 50×), 1 mM N‑Acetyl‑L‑Cystein (1 mL of 500 mM stock), 10 mM Nicotinamide (10 µL of 1 M stock), 1 mM R‑Spondin CM (10 mL of 10 % stock). Total volume 100 mL. Store at 4 °C for ≤1 week.

Branching Medium (BM): combine 0.2 mM 2‑Phospho‑L‑Ascorbic Acid Trisodium Salt (10 µL), 0.1 µM Dexamethasone (10 µL), 100 ng/mL DKK1 (20 µL of 50 µg/mL stock), 20 ng/mL EGF (20 µL of 50 µg/mL stock), 14 mM Glucose (4 µL of 1.4 M stock), 20 mM HEPES (20 µL of 1 M stock), 1 % ITS+ (20 µL of 100×), 10 mM Nicotinamide (10 µL of 1 M stock), 0.2 % Pen‑Strep (100 µL of 10 000 U/mL), 10 % R‑Spondin CM (10 mL), 17 mM Sodium Bicarbonate (200 µL of 850 mM stock), 6.3 mM Sodium Pyruvate (630 µL of 100 mM stock), 2 mM UltraGlutamine (100 µL of 200 mM stock), 76 % William‑E Medium (7.606 mL). Total volume 10 mL. Store at 4 °C for ≤1 week.
Freezing Medium (FM): combine 20 % FBS (2 mL), 10 % DMSO (1 mL), 70 % ADV+++ (7 mL). Total volume 10 mL. Store at –20 °C for up to 1 year.

After preparation, filter each medium through a 0.22 µm filter, aliquot as needed, and keep all media (except FM) at 4 °C for no longer than the times indicated above. Warm all media to 37 °C before adding to organoid cultures.

steps.title: Optional: Manual BRCO clone picking and passage
steps.instruction: Select branching organoid clones from mixed cultures, isolate them, and re‑embed for continued growth.

substeps.instruction: Place 9 mL ice‑cold ADV+++ in a 15 mL tube and keep on ice for the entire procedure.
Remove the Branching Medium (BM) from the well and add 1 mL ice‑cold ADV+++ directly to the well to dissolve the BME dome by gentle resuspension and scraping (as done during routine passaging).
Add a second 1 mL of ice‑cold ADV+++ to the well and gently mix to increase spacing between cystic ICO and BRCO structures.

Using an inverted microscope (or an EVOS hybrid system for dense cultures >70 % BME occupation), visualize the suspension and pick individual branching structures with a sterile P200 pipette tip, avoiding any cystic ICO.
Transfer each picked structure back into the 15 mL ice‑cold ADV+++ tube; resuspend the pellet 5–7 times by pipetting to remove residual BME from the tip.
Repeat the picking cycle until all desired BRCO are collected; discard the original plate containing the remaining cystic ICO.
Centrifuge the collected BRCO suspension at 453 g for 5 min at 4 °C, carefully remove supernatant, and blot the pellet dry with a P200 tip.
Add fresh BME to the pellet to embed the clones in the same number of wells of a 12‑well suspension plate as the original culture, forming three 25 µL domes per well in a triangular arrangement.
Incubate the plate for 3 min at 21 °C–25 °C, then flip the plate smoothly to allow even distribution of organoids within the dome.
Incubate the flipped plate for 45 min at 37 °C.
Flip the plate back, add 1 mL pre‑warmed Branching Medium (BM) to each well by gently dispensing against the well side to avoid disturbing the domes.
Monitor cultures every 2–3 days; refresh with 1 mL pre‑warmed BM or passage as needed.
Maintain sterility throughout: work in a laminar flow cabinet when possible, wipe all surfaces with 70 % ethanol, wear gloves, and use sterile pipette tips.
